_comment: GRASS-FIELD. The camera-relative ground cover, and the flag that decides whether it or the baked scatter owns the ground plane. See scripts/world/grass_field.gd and shaders/grass_field.gdshader for the mechanism, and ralph/reports/WORLD_GRASS_2026-08-25.md for the measurement that forced it: a continuous carpet is ~40x outside the chapter's placement ceiling however it is spent, so no density number in vegetation.json reaches the reference. ALL OF THIS IS TUNABLE.
_comment_enabled: OFF BY DEFAULT, deliberately, and this is the whole safety story for the change. The one thing no container in this project can measure is the only hardware that matters -- PERF-ROG-GPU records that the Compatibility renderer counts MultiMesh batches rather than instances and that this box rasterises in software. So the owner has to be able to switch between the two ground systems on the Ally itself, and a bad handheld result has to be one boolean away from gone rather than a revert. Turn on to evaluate; do not turn on by default until a handheld pass says it is affordable.
_comment_suppress: Which vegetation.json layers vegetation.gd skips while the field is on, so the two systems never both dress the same ground. These four are the whole non-colliding carpet -- 625,227 of the 725,949 placements in the WORLD-GRASS bake, 86% of it. Everything NOT in this list stays scatter and must: you collide with trees, rocks and bushes, you harvest them, and they are the landmarks the eye navigates by. A shader carpet is the right instrument for the thing you walk through and the wrong one for the thing you walk into. ONE NAME IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT AND HAS TO BE ADDED ON CONSOLIDATION: ralph/WORLD-GRASS adds a `groundmat` layer (clover and a broadleaf, 145,577 placements) which is ground cover this field also replaces. This branch is cut from main, where that layer does not exist yet, and tests/test_grass_field.gd fails on a name that resolves to nothing -- correctly, because an erase of a missing key is silent and would leave both systems dressing the same ground. Whoever lands the two branches together adds "groundmat" here.
_comment_ring: The ring's size and how it is populated. `tuft_count` is the ONLY number that decides how much geometry exists -- it does not grow with the world, which is the entire point of the approach. `centre_bias` below 1.0 crowds tufts toward the middle: r = radius * pow(randf(), bias), so 0.5 is a uniform disc and lower values spend more of the budget where the camera actually is. A uniform disc wastes most of its tufts in the outer ring where they are sub-pixel.
_comment_snap: Metres the ring snaps to as it follows the camera. Not cosmetic: the coverage noise is evaluated in WORLD space while the instances live in LOCAL space, so a continuously-following ring re-rolls which tufts survive every frame and the whole field boils. Snapping means the set only changes when the ring has crossed a cell. Larger is steadier and coarser at the ring's outer edge.
_comment_blade: One tuft is `blades_per_tuft` tapered strips at different yaws, generated in code by grass_field.gd::_tuft_mesh -- no asset enters the repository, which keeps CLAUDE.md's no-new-assets rule for the Meadows untouched. `blade_segments` is how many quads make a blade; more bends more smoothly and costs triangles linearly. Heights are in metres against the 1.80m trainer: WORLD-GRASS landed the scattered tufts at a 0.71m mean and a blind critic still called them short, so this starts a little above that and grows with distance so a far blade stays a few pixels tall instead of shimmering.
_comment_coverage: What stops this being a lawn. `density_gain` is the flat keep-chance; `clump_scale` is the frequency of the drift noise that modulates it (smaller is broader drifts) and `clump_contrast` how hard that noise bites -- 0 is uniform coverage, 1 is drifts with genuinely bare ground between them. This is where GROUND-LAYERS' measured composition target lives now: roughly 70% open grass, 15% path/worn, 10% low accents, 5% special. That target was expressed as placement counts before and cannot be any more, so it is expressed as noise here. TUNABLE, and the first thing to re-judge against a blind pass.
_comment_colour: Derived from measurement, not by eye. Sampled off-route on WORLD-GRASS's own frames, the meadow's ground reads #798732 (hue 68.3, value 0.529) against the owner reference's foreground grass at #7c8737 (hue 68.4, value 0.529) -- the palette was already right, so these sit around it rather than replacing it. `ground_blend` is the fix for the defect three blind rounds named: it mixes the terrain's OWN colour map into the base of every blade, so growth appears to come out of the ground instead of standing on a picture of it. `translucency` fakes the light through a blade; the Compatibility renderer has no subsurface scattering, so it lifts the tip rather than pretending to transmit.
_comment_wind: Free here, and the owner's reference frames are of moving grass. Strength is in metres of tip travel.
_comment_gust: GUST-WAVE. A travelling front on top of the ambient breeze, rather than the whole field leaning together -- which reads as a wobble where a gust crossing the meadow reads as weather. `gust_speed` is metres per second of front travel and `gust_length` its wavelength in metres, so 7.0 and 26.0 is a front crossing the visible field about every four seconds. Free: it is one sine over a dot product the shader already has. The owner reference frames are of moving grass and this is the half of that motion a per-item noise cannot give.
_comment_stones: STONE-FIELD. Loose grit, gravel and field stone, on the SAME camera-relative ring as the grass and storing nothing either. It exists because a blind pass, asked directly whether stones, path edges and tree bases read as bedded into the ground or sitting on top of it, answered: 'No -- everything sits on top. This is the single most consistent failure in the set.' It measured the band-4 cobbles as flat-topped slabs with their entire edge exposed, none partially buried, none casting a contact shadow; and it found the path shares one texture with the meadow, 'so the boundary is a density edge rather than a material edge, and it looks cut', with a surface that at 1-3m is 'a repeating mottled blob pattern with no grain, gravel, dirt clod, rut or footprint'. This is the path's own surface and the answer to both. `ground` names where stone is ALLOWED and is built from the same terrain texture list the grass field builds its FORBIDDEN mask from, so the two are inverses by construction and tile the ground between them. `stray_chance` is what stops the gravel ending on the same hard line the grass mask was criticised for -- a few field stones out on ordinary meadow. `sink` is the whole bedded argument in one number: the fraction of its own height a stone is buried, so its lower edge is under the surface instead of standing proud of it all the way round. `contact_darken` is the occlusion a stone this small will never get from the shadow map. TUNABLE, and the whole tier is one `enabled` away from gone.
_comment_cover_tiers: The generic plant tiers on the same ring: small bushes, flower drifts, forest litter. Each is one MultiMesh child running shaders/cover_tier.gdshader, differing only by mesh and numbers -- see that shader's header for the rule about WHAT may be generated this way. Short version: a tier qualifies only if it does not collide, carries no persistent state, is small enough that appearing at the ring's edge is invisible, and exists in numbers too large to store. Trees and boulders fail three of those -- they are landmarks, they stop the camera's SpringArm, and they must be where you left them. HARVESTABLE bushes fail the state test: vegetation.json's `bushes` layer carries harvest_item fiber, and harvesting needs an identity that survives, which a thing that does not exist until the camera nears it cannot have. So these bushes are DECORATIVE understorey and the harvestable ones stay scattered. tests/test_grass_field.gd enforces that half of the rule against vegetation.json directly. Each tier draws from its own RNG stream so adding or removing one cannot reshuffle where any other tier's items land.

cover_tiers._why: Small bushes. A blind pass found the world jumps from 50cm grass straight to 6m canopy with nothing between -- 'a forest you can see straight through at knee height' -- and counted two mid-height plants across twelve frames. This is that missing band. Sparse and heavily drifted on purpose: understorey gathers, it does not carpet, and the meadow's negative space is what GROUND-LAYERS measured as worth keeping.
cover_tiers.name: bushes

cover_tiers._why: Flower drifts. The defect this answers was measured rather than judged: a blind pass counted flowers appearing EXACTLY TWICE in twelve frames, both the same violet bush asset, each 'a single isolated ball of saturated violet with a hard base', against moong-02 running a pink drift across ~40% of frame width and the keyart putting purple, gold and white wildflowers in every panel. The numbers here are shaped by that: a LOW drift_scale (0.03) means broad patches rather than a sprinkle, and a high drift_contrast means genuinely empty ground between them. Prompt 72 asked for the same thing in its own words -- 'the reference pink drifts are tight and irregular'. Colour is the one place this tier deliberately leaves the meadow palette: palette.json reserves flower_gold #d9b340 as an accent and the keyart carries lilac, so the bloom is lilac over an olive stalk. It is NOT oxblood and must never drift toward it -- that red is reserved for Team Tether and three blind passes have confirmed the reservation is still clean.
cover_tiers.name: flowers

cover_tiers._why: Forest litter. Band 2 is called forest floor and a blind pass found it carrying meadow grass and sand under the trees -- 'no leaf litter, no needles, no moss, no fungi, no fallen branches' -- and separately that 'a player walking these four bands would not know the region had changed'. This is the band-differentiating dressing, and it is restricted to the forest_floor ground type so it appears where the terrain already says there are trees rather than being scattered everywhere and hoping. slope_lie 1.0 lays it ON the ground following the gradient, which is what makes litter read as litter and not as flat cards standing on a slope; sway 0 because leaves on the ground do not move in a breeze.
cover_tiers.name: litter

_comment_forbidden: Ground the field refuses, by terrain texture NAME rather than by id. terrain_playground.json's `textures` array order is what assigns the ids (0 grass, 1 soil, 2 rock, 3 path, 4 damp, 5 forest_floor), so naming them means a lane that reorders that list does not silently move the mask onto the wrong surface. `path` is what keeps the routes readable -- the same control map the terrain paints its dirt from, so the verge lines up with the road for free instead of being a second exclusion rule that has to be kept in sync.
